sources.name: NISAR L2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV), L-band
sources.provider: NASA / ISRO, distributed by the Alaska Satellite Facility DAAC
sources.license: Open data (NASA Earth Science Data policy)
sources.used_for: The core of the project: HH and HV backscatter for 10 dates (track 172, frame 168, ascending), classified into open water and flooded vegetation.
sources.processing: Streamed over the AOI only, converted to dB, despeckled (Quegan & Yu 2001), thresholded. See meta.json.

sources.name: NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS): NISAR GCOV browse imagery, OPERA Dynamic Surface Water Extent (DSWx-HLS), MODIS Aqua corrected reflectance
sources.provider: NASA EOSDIS (OPERA products by NASA JPL)
sources.license: Open data; NASA asks for acknowledgement of GIBS
sources.used_for: Live reference map layers, shown unmodified next to our own classification.
sources.processing: None. Tiles are requested from NASA by the browser.
sources.acknowledgement: We acknowledge the use of imagery provided by services from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), part of NASA's Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS).

sources.name: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) monthly precipitation, PRECTOTCORR
sources.used_for: Rainfall in the Angolan headwaters that feeds the flood.
sources.processing: Mean of three points; Nov-Apr totals per year.

sources.name: Water Observations from Space (WOfS) annual summary, from USGS/NASA Landsat
sources.used_for: Open-water extent of every year 1984-2025, the long-term context NISAR cannot give yet.
sources.processing: Cropped to the AOI at 120 m; yearly areas. See history.json.

sources.name: JRC Global Surface Water v1.5, occurrence 1984-2024
sources.license: Copernicus open licence; cite Pekel et al. 2016, Nature 540
sources.citation: Pekel, J.-F., Cottam, A., Gorelick, N., Belward, A. S. (2016). High-resolution mapping of global surface water and its long-term changes. Nature 540, 418-422.
sources.used_for: How often each pixel was open water over 40 years.
sources.processing: Cropped to the AOI, averaged to 80 m.

sources.name: GloFAS river discharge reanalysis
sources.provider: Copernicus Emergency Management Service / ECMWF, accessed through the Open-Meteo Flood API
sources.used_for: Modelled inflow of the Okavango River near Mohembo.

sources.name: Scientific references
items: Quegan, S., Yu, J. J. (2001). Filtering of multichannel SAR images. IEEE Trans. Geosci. Remote Sens. 39(11), 2373-2379.
Inman, V. L., Lyons, M. B. (2020). Automated inundation mapping over large areas using Landsat data and Google Earth Engine. Remote Sensing 12(8), 1348.

Wolski, P., Murray-Hudson, M., Thito, K., Cassidy, L. (2017). Keeping it simple: monitoring flood extent in large data-poor wetlands using MODIS SWIR data. Int. J. Appl. Earth Obs. Geoinf. 57, 224-234.

tools.used_for: Writing and reviewing the Python data pipeline and the serverless assistant function, checking data sources, drafting documentation.
tools.human_check: Every number in the app is computed by the published pipeline from the cited data, not written by an AI.

tools.tool: OpenAI GPT-5.4 mini via API; open-weight gpt-oss models on Groq as backup
tools.human_check: It may only answer from assistant_context.json, a file generated from our data. It is not trained or fine-tuned by us.

ai.not_ai: No AI-generated images, video or audio are used. All maps are rendered from satellite data. No NASA logo or insignia is used.
ai.in_app_label: AI-generated answer based on this project's data files. It can be wrong: check the numbers against the charts.
